cases.setup: Synthetic accepted offers: funded at 5000 cents and unfunded; owning client, selected artist, other client, other artist and anonymous caller.
cases.action: Call mine, upload, submit, requestRevision, approve and file read as each caller.
cases.expected: Only participants read delivery state; only selected artist uploads/submits for the funded offer; only owning client requests revisions/approves. Unauthorized file reads reject without bytes. Unfunded offers cannot enter delivery/review.

cases.setup: Funded offer at version 0; valid supported images.
cases.action: Stage an original and two process images; submit with expectedVersion 0. Repeat on a separate offer with three process images.
cases.expected: Each complete set publishes atomically as version 1 awaiting review, with preview and all process images available to participants.

cases.setup: Funded offer with a previously readable state.
cases.action: Attempt submission with missing original, zero/one/four process images, duplicate process IDs, wrong-kind IDs, another offer's IDs and invalid image inputs; interrupt an upload, then retry valid delivery.
cases.expected: Invalid or incomplete sets never become ready. Prior state and files remain available; retry succeeds without extra versions or revision consumption.

cases.setup: Valid JPEG, PNG and WebP originals with recognizable content; existing image limits supplied by the implementation harness.
cases.action: Upload supported images and inputs that violate format, content or size limits.
cases.expected: Supported images within existing limits succeed; invalid inputs reject. Generated preview visibly depicts the original, has a visible watermark and reduced dimensions. Original bytes remain unchanged.

cases.action: Inspect client-facing responses; read preview/process/original as both participants and outsiders; attempt cross-offer and staged-file access.
cases.expected: Participants can read published preview/process files. Owning client cannot read original before approval. Outsiders receive no delivery files. Client-facing data contains no public storage URLs or original file identifiers before approval; staging IDs remain scoped to the authorized artist.

cases.action: Client requests revision with an instruction; artist submits complete replacement using the current version. Repeat once.
cases.expected: Requests attach to versions 1 and 2; replacement submissions become versions 2 and 3. Notes and version history persist. Each request consumes exactly one revision; each replacement requires the full file set.

cases.setup: A revision has been requested; replacement has not been submitted.
cases.action: Request another revision or approve the old delivery; then submit the replacement and review it.
cases.expected: Old delivery cannot receive another review decision while replacement is pending. New submitted version becomes reviewable.

cases.action: Request a third revision, then approve version 3.
cases.expected: Third request rejects without changing history/count. Approval succeeds for version 3.

cases.action: Approve/requestRevision using version 1; upload/submit using stale expectedVersion.
cases.expected: Stale operations cannot change current version, phase, history, revision count, approved version or release records.

cases.setup: Latest version awaiting review; saved offer amount is 5000 cents.
cases.expected: Exactly that version becomes approved; exactly one simulated release records 5000 cents. Artist sees approved version and simulated payout amount. Client receives approved original and agreed written licence.

cases.setup: Approved version with earlier submitted versions.
cases.action: Download each version's original as the client; retry approval, revision, upload and submission.
cases.expected: Client downloads only approved version's unchanged original. Later actions cannot replace approved version or create another release; unauthorized originals remain inaccessible.

cases.action: Reload client and artist sessions and re-read authoritative state through fresh requests.
cases.expected: Versions, notes, revision count, phase, approved version, 5000-cent release and stored licence survive reload. Approved download remains available.

cases.setup: Current version awaiting review; synchronized callers.
cases.action: Replay and concurrently issue approvals for the same version.
cases.expected: One approval transition and one 5000-cent release maximum. Retries may return existing success or conflict, but approved version and release remain identical.

cases.setup: Current version awaiting review with revisions remaining.
cases.action: Replay and concurrently issue revision requests for the same version.
cases.expected: Exactly one request is accepted into history and count increases once. Duplicate calls cannot overwrite the accepted note or consume another revision.

cases.setup: Two different complete staged sets for the same current version.
cases.action: Submit both concurrently and replay the winning submission.
cases.expected: Only one next version publishes, containing one coherent file set. No mixed files, skipped version or duplicate publication.

cases.setup: Current version awaiting review with a revision remaining.
cases.action: Race approval against revision request for that version; repeat with reversed scheduling.
cases.expected: Exactly one transition wins. Approval implies one release and no revision consumption; revision implies one consumed revision and no release.

cases.setup: Controlled failure injection around publication and approval persistence.
cases.action: Fail a write before completion, then retry through a fresh request.
cases.expected: No partial ready delivery or approved state without its corresponding release. Retry yields one coherent committed result and at most one release.

cases.setup: Synthetic client and artist sessions in the Brazilian Portuguese workspace, desktop and narrow widths.
cases.action: Complete delivery, preview/process inspection, two revisions, approval and final download; reload both views.
cases.expected: Controls reflect role, phase and revision limit, remain usable at both widths, and show version, notes, simulated amount and approved download correctly. Manual approval needs no expiry timer.

redStrategy.baseline: Use only synthetic fixtures funded through test-only setup. Execute behavioral checks against runnable operations and the workspace.
redStrategy.observableFailure: Before implementation, demonstrate missing or rejected valid delivery operations, absent review controls, inaccessible expected files, incorrect persisted state, unauthorized bytes, or incorrect release/count invariants. Missing endpoints count as explicit runtime capability failures.
redStrategy.avoid: Do not use unresolved imports, compilation/type errors or deliberately broken tests as red evidence.
redStrategy.concurrency: Synchronize competing requests at the transition boundary; inspect authoritative state, history and release count afterward. Exercise both winner orderings.
redStrategy.verification: After behavioral checks, run the existing suite, typecheck and optimized build; build failures are separate from behavioral red evidence.

limitations: The supplied spec is draft revision 0.1 and presents licence and execution-path decisions for review; these files alone do not establish approval.

If the fixed licence is approved, assert personal use and personal-profile display with artist credit, exclusions for commercial use/resale/transfer, retained artist copyright, artist visibility before first delivery, client visibility before approval and identical agreed terms with final download.
Numeric image limits, note-length rules, watermark dimensions and exact error responses are unspecified. Reuse established limits without inventing thresholds.
Artist access to originals, direct replay response shape and licence transport are not fully specified; assert only the stated access and state invariants.
Failure-injection tests require a test-only persistence seam; reload verifies saved behavior but does not alone prove process-restart durability.

No linked files, other files, network, accounts, credentials, collaboration or resource tools were accessed. Actual Pix webhook verification, provider payouts, refunds, AI flags, scheduling, expiry and deployment remain outside this design.
